h1: Chiang Mai travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Chiang Mai is a Thailand base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, add Chiang Mai Old City, and use Wat Chedi Luang to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Chiang Mai International handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with Old City for the easiest first Chiang Mai stay, then compare Nimmanhaemin and Night Bazaar when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Chiang Mai hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use Old City for sightseeing, Nimmanhaemin for a different local base, and Night Bazaar or Riverside when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Chiang Mai unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Old City for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave extra time for Chiang Mai International, especially for early flights, late arrivals, traffic or unfamiliar transfer routes.

travelTips.title: Local movement
travelTips.text: Plan each day in clusters around Wat Phra That Doi Suthep and Chiang Mai Old City so transfers do not consume the best sightseeing hours.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Keep one flexible slot for nearby routes from Chiang Mai, checking weather, transport and opening hours before committing.

history.text: Mangrai founded Chiang Mai in 1294 or 1296 on a site that the Lawa people called Wiang Nopburi.
With the decline of Lan Na, Chiang Mai lost importance and was occupied by the Toungoo Empire in 1556.
It formally became part of the Thonburi Kingdom in 1774, by an agreement with Kawila, after the Thonburi king Taksin helped drive out the Burmese.
First covering just 17.5 square kilometres (6.8 sq mi), the city was enlarged to 40.2 square kilometres (15.5 sq mi) on 5 April 1983.
The first revision of such an updated urban area (Thai: เขตเมือง) was published in 1989, with the second one following in 1999.
In May 2006, Chiang Mai was the site of the Chiang Mai Initiative, concluded between ASEAN and the "ASEAN+3" countries, (China, Japan, and South Korea).
The third revision from 2012 expands the old municipal city border inside Muaeng Chiang Mai district to Mae Rim in the north, San Kamphaeng and Doi Saket in the east, Hang Dong and Saraphi.
Chiang Mai was one of two tourist destinations in Thailand on TripAdvisor's 2014 list of "25 Best Destinations in the World", where it stood at number 24.
As of 2022, a fourth revision of Chiang Mai's urban area is under way and currently up for debate by the public.
